_doc: Ledger 0080: the San Diego freeway network on Lake Murray v4's engine, beside the original (tracks/san-diego-freeway, airoso's network engine; its config is PR 34's, b888f10). Phase 1 = the line: I 8 eastbound end to end (the original's network.reference_line), its six declared decks, through the LM chain (tools/ship_track.sh, ship.json engine lm-v4). The other carriageways, ramps, flyovers and barriers are phase 2 (the ledger's map). Phase 2a adds I 8 westbound as a connector (ledger 0080 phase 2).
name: San Diego Freeway Free Roam (LM engine)
author: doooom

location._anchor: I-8 in Mission Valley (straight WB stretch near the SR-163 stack) - AC_START snaps to the nearest freeway edge here. (project_freeway_net's spawn rule, build_network_mesh._freeroam_dummies. Since 2026-11-01 the chain's network_reference step replaces that dummies.json: the grid at the START of network.reference_line, AC_TIME_0 at its finish, fleet/LAWS.md L11; lat/lon here still feed the lighting.)

source._doc: the line, its 3DEP and its widths come from the original's final network draft (lm_intake below); this track fetches nothing

route._divided_double_doc: one carriageway, one direction of travel: no yellow centre line; white lane dividers stay (route.lane_dividers absent = on)
route._edge_doc: a freeway has no curb and no sidewalk: the rally ports' near-zero edge (ledger 0078 round 8). The real edge is a paved shoulder to a concrete barrier; the barrier is owed (ledger 0080 map), so phase 1 lays none rather than an invented one.

_default_width_m_doc: the source config's (scripts.config needs it); the line carries its own per-vertex widths, which the assembler sweeps

scenery._draft_lamps_doc: v021's 55 m street lamps are a neighbourhood's; the freeway's lighting is not measured here

layouts.name: Freeway Free Roam (LM engine)
layouts.run: Point to point: Interstate 8 eastbound, end to end inside the box; I 8 westbound alongside (a connector, driven by drive_test --line network)

lm_intake._source_data_doc: ledger 0080: the original's FINAL network draft (PR 34's scripts at b888f10, run on the Mac), not its committed data/ (the PC's first run, before PR 34's fixes). tools/network_line.py wrote it; its network_line.json has the provenance and md5s.
lm_intake._grid_crop_m_doc: [invented] 1,000 m of the 3DEP grid round the line (phase 1 builds the line alone; the source grid is the whole 18 x 15 km network box and the assembler never finished on it in 45 min). The extent of the scenery, not a geometry value: no sample moves. Phase 2 (the network) needs the whole box, and terrain.tiers. fleet/GATES-CHANGELOG.md 2026-11-05.
lm_intake._width_taper_doc: ledger 0078 round 5 (Milford), the rally ports' rate: a width step in the source line (the network draft's per-edge lane widths step at every edge joint: 7.16 -> 10.82 m at s 25 built a twisted quad and 14 ground-on-top samples) becomes a flare, widening only. The rate is that entry's, not measured here.
lm_intake._connectors_doc: ledger 0080 phase 2: the network's other carriageways as connectors, read from source/network-draft-pr34/connectors.local.json (tools/network_connectors.py, from lm_intake.network_connectors below: the draft's own edges, the line's resolver, each carriageway's own 3DEP, the decks from the lidar)
lm_intake._network_connectors_doc: phase 2a: I 8 westbound. Each entry is resolved by scripts.geometry.network_reference.resolve (the line's resolver) on the network draft; the record carries its decks (lidar, deck_profiles.lidar.json) and a one-way paint. Regenerate with python tools/network_connectors.py <network-draft-project> tracks/san-diego-freeway/source/network-draft-pr34 tracks/san-diego-freeway-lm/track.config.json
lm_intake._grid_upsample_doc: [invented value; existing key, ledger 0078] the cut 3DEP grid pre-divided x2 (bilinear: the same samples, finer facets; with the assembler x2 the ground is 13.75 m facets, not 27.5 m). Phase 2a measured it: with I 8 westbound beside the line the 27.5 m ground stood over the lanes between the carriageways (ground on top 1,119 line / 1,224 WB samples) and 138 / 130 at 13.75 m.
